main_text.p: Item[?] pulverem peste correptis statim morbi initio potui exhibent,vel stibium, more chymistarum paratum. His quoq; non minus explodendi veniunt infani Paracelsi-stae, & illi omnes,quicunque sint,qui ele-bori nigri abstractum pestiferis potadum propinant.Etenim immoderatius furfum, deorsumq; corpus exagitat haec omnia,ac Propterea[?] vires nimiopere dissoluunt. Quin etiam Moibani antidotum, licet ad omnia propemodum venenorum genera caeteris praestet, quoniam tame immoderate quoq; vacuat, & vires resoluit, nequaq; in hoc affectu probare possumus. Propterea si sta-tim initio aegre,aut non satis euomunt pe-ste correpti,tunc potione aquae tepidae sy-rupo acetato simplici immistum (facta fri-ctione in gyrum circa os uentriculi) excita-bitur uomitus.At si ab alui,pfluvio[?] incho-at pestilens febris, detergente clystere ju-vanda est natura.Quoniam quo natura vergit,eo vacuandum est. Quod si morbi ini-tio huiusmodi excretiones haud contin-guit,statim iniecto,& reiecto clystere emol-liente, detrahetur sanguis, si vires ferant: quandoquidem morbus peracutus est, & extremos habet labores, atq; celerrime ad

page.notes: Printed text is set in one continuous paragraph, no indents visible. Left margin top: first word partly cut off at the scan edge, read as "Item" with [?]. The word beginning the line "Propterea" has an ornamental first letter that I could not read with certainty. "alui,pfluvio" has a mark between "alui" and "pfluvio" that is uncertain. "(facta fri-ctione" spacing may differ from print. Long s rendered as plain s throughout; u/v and i/j normalised as instructed.
